title: Mathematics — 18 November 2026 announcement batch: 11 notable recent papers
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred ordering of notable papers, not a popularity ranking, and citation evidence is limited for papers this new.

sections.title: The Zaks--Perles--Wills volume conjecture I: three-dimensional lattice polytopes
sections.abstract: For full-dimensional three-dimensional lattice polytopes with k >= 3 interior lattice points, the authors prove a volume bound 6(k+1), characterize equality by a specific Sylvester simplex, and thereby complete the conjecture in dimension three together with known k = 1, 2 cases.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.2 states that a full-dimensional lattice polytope P in R^3 with k >= 3 interior lattice points has volume at most 6(k+1), with equality exactly for affine-unimodular copies of conv(0, 2e1, 3e2, 6(k+1)e3); the inequality is strict when minimum lattice width is at least three.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Three-dimensional full-dimensional lattice polytopes; k is the number of interior lattice points. Equality is classified up to affine-unimodular equivalence.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper proves the three-dimensional case; the conjecture in dimensions four and higher remains unresolved.

sections.title: The Bessis Moussa Villani conjecture in finite von Neumann algebras
sections.abstract: The authors extend the Bessis–Moussa–Villani positivity and Laplace-representation result from matrix algebras to bounded operators in finite von Neumann algebras with a faithful normal trace, using tracial spectral measures.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem A states nonnegativity of traces of symmetrized words for positive operator pairs and gives a positive-measure Laplace representation of the trace exponential.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Bounded operators in a finite von Neumann algebra equipped with a faithful normal tracial state; the positivity assertion takes positive A and B.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is scoped to finite algebras with the specified trace; it does not claim the same theorem for arbitrary operator algebras or nontracial states.

sections.title: New bounds on simplex-avoiding sets in two dimensions
sections.abstract: The authors study measurable sets avoiding finite geometric configurations and give upper bounds of 7/11 for orthonormal-basis-free subsets of S^2 and 9/16 for unit-equilateral-triangle-free subsets of R^2.
sections.claimed_result: Theorems 1.1–1.2 prove the bounds 7/11 for normalized spherical measure and 9/16 for upper Banach density, using geometric fractional chromatic-number bounds from finite probes.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Measurable sets exclude the specified configurations; the plane result concerns upper Banach density. The two finite probes have 15 and 14 points, respectively.
sections.unique_caveat: These are upper bounds, not exact extremal densities; for the plane problem, the paper notes a conjectured optimal density of 1/2.

sections.title: A counterexample to the one-supremum conjecture and sharp logarithmic weighted bounds for Calderón--Zygmund operators
sections.abstract: The author disproves a strong-type one-supremum conjecture using explicit weights, then proves matching logarithmically corrected upper and lower growth bounds for Calderón–Zygmund operators, identifying the optimal common logarithmic exponent.
sections.claimed_result: For every 1 < p < infinity, the proposed no-log bound fails for a fixed Hilbert transform; the paper establishes a logarithmically corrected bound and claims the common exponent gamma_p = max(1/p, 1/p') is optimal.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The strong-type one-supremum formulation with mixed A_p–A_infinity characteristics evaluated on the same cube; explicit weights and fixed singular-integral operators.
sections.unique_caveat: The counterexample concerns that stated weighted formulation; it does not rule out different bounds under different hypotheses or formulations.

sections.title: Cutoff on abelian groups
sections.abstract: For abelian random walks whose inverse minimum jump probability is at most logarithmic in group size, the authors prove that cutoff is equivalent to the product condition, give a sharp mixing-window estimate, and construct near-threshold examples without cutoff.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove a quantitative mixing-window bound and show that, when the inverse smallest nonzero jump rate is O(log |G|), cutoff holds exactly when the product condition holds; reversibility is not assumed.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Sequences of continuous-time random walks on finite abelian groups; the equivalence uses the logarithmic sparsity condition on the jump distribution.
sections.unique_caveat: The equivalence is not asserted outside that sparsity regime; the paper constructs abelian Cayley-graph examples beyond the threshold where the product condition does not imply cutoff.

sections.title: Sidorenko Inequalities in Oriented Graphs
sections.abstract: The authors define relative Sidorenko and anti-Sidorenko inequalities for oriented graphs against arbitrary oriented host graphs, characterize the connected relatively Sidorenko class, and give families of examples of both types.
sections.claimed_result: For a connected oriented graph with at least one arc, the authors prove it is relatively Sidorenko exactly when it is a one-way orientation of a reversible weakly norming graph; they also exhibit relatively anti-Sidorenko families.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The homomorphism inequalities must hold for every oriented host graph with the specified underlying graph; the characterization is for connected oriented graphs with an arc.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors note that a structural characterization of weakly norming graphs themselves remains open.

sections.title: Sharp Fractional Capacitary-Distance Hardy Inequalities
sections.abstract: For open subsets of R^d and a stated fractional Sobolev parameter range, the authors prove a capacitary-distance Hardy inequality and establish sharpness of its alpha-exponent and smoothness range.
sections.claimed_result: For alpha in (0,1], open Omega subset R^d, p in (1,infinity), and s in (0,min(1+1/p,d/p)), the authors prove integral_Omega |u(x)|^p/d_alpha,s,p(x)^(sp) dx <= C alpha^(-p') [u]_(s,p)^p for u in C_c^infinity(Omega), with C depending only on d,s,p; they report sharpness of the alpha exponent and parameter range.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Fractional capacity distance is defined relative to the complement of an arbitrary open set; the inequality is stated for compactly supported smooth functions and the specified fractional Sobolev parameters.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is stated for u in C_c^infinity(Omega) and the indicated parameter range; broader function spaces are not asserted in the abstract.

sections.title: Regularity of solutions to complex Monge-Ampere equations in big classes
sections.abstract: On a compact Kähler manifold, the authors obtain local C^{2,alpha} regularity for a non-pluripolar complex Monge-Ampere equation in an arbitrary big class under either of two stated conditions on the log density, including a smooth positive density case.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract claims local C^{2,alpha} regularity on the ample locus under a weighted Laplacian lower bound on the log density, or under a quasi-plurisubharmonic decomposition; smooth positive density yields a smooth solution there, without nefness.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Non-pluripolar complex Monge-Ampere equation on a compact Kähler manifold in an arbitrary big class; regularity is local to the ample locus and depends on the stated data hypotheses.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated regularity is on the ample locus; it is not a regularity claim across its complement.

sections.title: An improved bound on the strong chromatic index via local flag algebras
sections.abstract: Using a local flag algebra method, the author proves that every graph with sufficiently large maximum degree Delta has strong chromatic index at most 1.642 Delta^2, improving the previous stated bound of 1.73 Delta^2.
sections.claimed_result: For every graph G of sufficiently large maximum degree Delta, the author proves chi'_s(G) <= 1.642 Delta^2.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite graphs with sufficiently large maximum degree; strong edge coloring requires distinct colors for edges that are incident or joined by a third edge.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is asymptotic in maximum degree and gives an upper bound, not an exact strong chromatic index.

sections.title: Second-class particle in ASEP. Rarefaction fan
sections.abstract: For ASEP on the integer lattice, the authors derive a fixed-time position-distribution formula for a second-class particle under arbitrary initial conditions and obtain a rarefaction-fan limit extending the TASEP result of Cator–Pimentel.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove a general formula for the particle's position distribution at any fixed time for arbitrary initial conditions, then derive its limiting distribution in the rarefaction-fan case.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Asymmetric simple exclusion process on the integer lattice; the limiting-distribution application is in the rarefaction-fan regime.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract identifies the rarefaction-fan limit as the application; it does not state a corresponding asymptotic formula for all initial regimes.

sections.title: An inexact stochastic variance-reduced gradient method for constrained convex finite-sum optimization
sections.abstract: For constrained convex finite-sum problems, the authors propose an inexact SVRG method that improves first-order oracle complexity for solutions with deterministically bounded constraint violation and expected optimality gap, and give a deterministic conic-optimization specialization.
sections.claimed_result: The authors propose an inexact SVRG algorithm that improves the best-known first-order oracle complexity for epsilon-surely-feasible stochastic optimization, and derive a deterministic first-order method when the objective has one summand.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Constrained convex finite-sum optimization; an epsilon-SFSO solution has deterministic constraint violation at most epsilon and expected optimality gap at most epsilon.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract reports only preliminary numerical results; practical advantage depends on constraint-gradient and cone-projection costs relative to objective-gradient evaluation.
